title: Adaptive prefetch rate-limiter + graceful precision guard for fast-path fallbacks
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Introduces an adaptive KV prefetch rate limiter and a 'graceful precision guard' safe-mode to reduce fast-path fallbacks and mitigate correctness regressions under bursty workloads. Telemetry added for prefetch/backpressure events and kernel-compat routing. Backwards compatible runtime flag controls rollout.
description:
Context and motivation: Production traces showed recurring tail regressions where the fast-path (FP16/quantized kernels) would be selected optimistically, then fail kernel-compat checks at runtime (kernel not available or mis-matched layout). That resulted in synchronous fallback to a slower path and spikes in latency for affected requests. Existing mitigations (aggressive prefetch + immediate fallback) either over-consumed GPU memory or exposed correctness risk when precision mismatches occurred. This PR introduces two coordinated controls to reduce observed regressions while preserving throughput: (1) an adaptive prefetch rate-limiter on the KV cache prefetcher that throttles speculative prefetches based on recent miss/fallback signals and GPU memory pressure, and (2) a "graceful precision guard" safe-mode that toggles per-model precision hints and prefers conservative kernels when instability is detected.
High-level summary of changes:
* Add prefetch_rate_limiter module to serving/runtime with token-bucket based pacing, backoff and a sliding window misprediction counter.
* Introduce model-level "precision_hint" (e.g., prefer_float16, prefer_int8, conservative) which is advisory and used by the scheduler and kernel selector to prefer compatible kernels.
* Add a safe-mode detector: if a given worker observes >X kernel-compat failures in Y minutes, it flips that model to graceful precision guard locally and emits telemetry.
* Tie the scheduler gating logic to both prefetch signals and precision_hint: when prefetcher is throttled, scheduler will avoid speculative KV prefetches for long sequences and will route to verified kernel variants first.
* Telemetry: new metrics prefetch_backoff_count, precision_guard_activations, kernel_compat_failures, and a tracing span for prefetch decisions.
* Config: runtime flags and per-model config to opt-in/out and tune thresholds.
Checklist (implemented):
- [x] Token-bucket prefetch limiter with exponential backoff
- [x] Precision hint plumbing from model manifest to scheduler
- [x] Safe-mode detector with local toggle and metric emission
- [x] Unit tests for limiter, hint propagation, and guard transitions
- [x] End-to-end perf canary job and microbench harness runs
- [x] Docs for runtime flags and sample model manifest entries
Commits (short):
- 1c0b7d: added prefetch rate limiter and unit tests
- 2a7f12: wire precision_hint through model manifest and API
- b3d99a: scheduler gating + kernel selector preference logic
- f5a44b: telemetry and tracing for prefetch/guard actions
- 9e8c21: docs and rollout plan
The files changed (high-level):
* serving/runtime/prefetch_limiter.py (+184/-12) - core token-bucket, backoff state, and unit tests
* serving/scheduler/kernel_selector.py (+120/-34) - added hint-aware selection logic and fallback counters
* serving/model/manifest.py (+60/-8) - new precision_hint field and parsing + validation
* serving/kv/cache_manager.py (+92/-46) - integrate limiter, expose API for scheduler to query prefetch state
* observability/metrics/telemetry_defs.yaml (+22) - new metric definitions
* docs/operator/precision-guard.md (+28/-0) - operator-facing guidance and tunables
* tests/e2e/prefetch_guard_canary.py (+26/-0) - canary harness and assertion thresholds
* examples/manifests/sample-precision-hints.yaml (+0/-0) - example manifest snippet
Example config snippet (from docs): {"model": "stable-text-2", "precision_hint": "conservative", "prefetch": {"enabled": true, "rate_limit_tokens_per_sec": 500}}
Testing and perf:
- Microbench on p3.2xlarge: 95th percentile tail latency reduced by 18% on a synthetic long-seq workload compared to baseline (no limiter).
- End-to-end canary (production trace replay): saw fast-path fallback rate drop from 0.9% -> 0.12% and throughput sustained within 3% of baseline.
- Memory utilization: average GPU memory footprint reduced slightly during bursts (7% lower peak), because speculative prefetches were curtailed.
Backwards compatibility and rollout:
- Default is opt-out: models keep previous behavior unless precision_hint or runtime flag is set.
- Central rollout: begin with conservative thresholds in prod for 2 weeks, then widen based on telemetry. The PR adds runtime flags to override enforcement for debugging.
Review conversation (high level, chronological):
- Marco Li (review): "This looks promising. Two questions: 1) any cost implications of additional telemetry? 2) are we exposing a way for users to opt out in managed (hosted) mode?"
- Asha (reply): "Telemetry is sparse counters and summaries; we sampled traces at 0.1% in the canary. Managed customers will see an opt-out toggle in the Console; default remains server-side. Added docs to clarify this."
- Jordan Kim (review): "The precision_hint is fine, but we should avoid making it a user footgun. Can we add validation to manifest parser and a warning in console?"
- Asha (reply): "Added manifest validation (reject unknown hints) and a console warning text proposal in docs/operator/precision-guard.md."
- Sofia Gonzalez (requested changes): "Please add unit coverage for the limiter's backoff state transition and a stress test where kernel-compat flips frequently."
- Asha (reply): "Added limiter backoff tests and an e2e stress scenario in tests/e2e/prefetch_guard_canary.py. See commit f5a44b."
CI history:
- Initial push: CI failed lint (pyflakes) on prefetch_limiter.py due to unused import; fixed in 1c0b7d -> rerun.
- Unit tests: pass (coverage for new modules >= 85%).
- Canary: ran nightlies and collected telemetry. Final CI status: pass. Merge strategy: squash-merge. Merged by release-bot after approvals.
Rollout notes:
- Feature gated via runtime flag: runtime.prefetch_limiter.enabled (false by default for on-prem customers upgrading without config change).
- Console: add toggle and recommended thresholds per workload.
- Follow-ups tracked in ENG-4199 (tune thresholds) and ENG-4234 (console UX).
Risk assessment and mitigation:
- Risk: overly conservative precision_guard may regress throughput. Mitigation: default is opt-out and the guard decays to previous state if performance impact is observed; we emit a metric precision_guard_perf_regressions.
- Risk: hidden interactions with autoscaler. Mitigation: added an integration test in perf-canary that replays scale-up events and validated no oscillation observed.
Notes for backports: This is safe to backport to v1.18.x (small surface area in scheduler and manifest parsing) but requires coordination for telemetry schema changes.
